cross_references.relationship: COORDINATED — Rees-Levering governs the form and content of the retail installment contract; §11711 governs fraud in the transaction. A conditional delivery that violated Rees-Levering disclosure requirements (§2983.2) = per se Rees-Levering violation + §11711 misrepresentation. Both claims can be pled against the same dealer on the same transaction. Rees-Levering §2983.2 provides a rescission right that runs alongside §11711 damages.

PARALLEL — §11711 applies to fraud in the licensed transaction itself; §17500 applies to advertising and representations leading up to the transaction. Wrong CARFAX = §11711 misrepresentation in the transaction + §17500 false advertising in the presentation of vehicle history. Both claims run against the dealer on the same facts.

COMMON LAW SUPPLEMENT — §11711 is the statutory dealer fraud remedy; §1709/§1710 is the common law fraud remedy. §11711 is easier to prove (no strict scienter) but capped at treble actual damages. §1709 + §3294 punitive is harder but has no cap. Plead both: §11711 as primary (lower bar); §1709/§3294 as punitive damages pathway.

FEDERAL CROSS-CLAIM — If the retail installment contract failed to disclose the conditional delivery contingency as a material financing term, federal TILA (15 U.S.C. §1638) provides a parallel federal civil remedy: actual damages + twice the finance charge + attorneys' fees. TILA SOL is 1 year — analyze tolling for 2018 transaction.
